demand.reason: Global scandium oxide production was about 80 tons in 2025, placing it far below the 500-ton threshold for negligible absolute demand.

growth.reason: Consumption is expanding rapidly, driven by emerging use-cases in scandium-stabilized zirconia electrolytes for solid oxide fuel cells and high-strength aluminum-scandium alloys for aerospace and additive manufacturing. Easing supply limits is accelerating growth well beyond a 12% CAGR.

supplier_concentration.reason:
Mining: Scandium is not mined as a primary product. It is extracted exclusively as a trace byproduct from titanium, zirconium, iron ore, and rare earth streams where China's dominant output controls over 85% of global mine supply (Score 5).


Refining: Refining circuits are fully integrated with primary byproduct processing plants. China dominates the chemical recovery and refinement of high-purity scandium oxide, exceeding the 85% global threshold (Score 5). Small volumes are also refined in Japan (from Philippine HPAL feed) and Canada (Rio Tinto, from titanium dioxide waste).

reserves.reason:
Time-frame: Scandium crustal resources are extensive. Known economic resources across identified global deposits represent many centuries of supply against a small 40-ton market, making the resource timeframe effectively limitless (>100 years).


Diversification: Scandium is exceptionally diffuse in the lithosphere and present across more than 100 minerals globally. Identified resources span Australia, Canada, China, Norway, Madagascar, and the US, with no single country holding a dominant 25% share, reflecting an HHI below 0.15 for highly distributed reserves.

end_use.reason:
Energy Generation & Grid (+1.5): scandium-stabilized zirconia is identified as the premier high-performance electrolyte for solid oxide fuel cells. Electrification & Transport (+1.0): lightweight aluminum-scandium alloys serve as high-performance structural materials in commercial aviation and additive manufacturing. Defense & National Security (+1.5): explicitly utilized in high-strength defense aerospace structures, tactical equipment components, and specialized military lighting guidance. Advanced Semiconductors & Computing (+1.0): used as a thin-film piezoelectric material (ScAlN) for advanced 5G RF filters and resonators.


Sector presence scores total 5.0 across 4 qualifying sectors. The breadth bonus for 4 sectors adds +1.5, yielding an objective composite score of 6.5.

substitutability_recyclability.reason:
Substitutability: Titanium alloys and carbon-fiber composites function as high-cost structural alternatives, and yttria-stabilized zirconia acts as a cheaper but lower-conductivity fuel cell substitute. True replacements for scandium's unique material performance carry significant trade-offs and require 3–5 years to adapt (Score 3).


Recyclability: Scandium is used in highly dissipative, low-concentration forms within alloy matrices, electronic films, and ceramics. Commercial recovery is non-existent, creating an effectively zero recycling scenario with no secondary supply chain active or foreseeable.

extraction_refining.reason: Scandium requires highly complex chemical separation circuits because it is retrieved only at parts-per-million levels from host leach solutions. Reaching a 99.99% pure oxide or distilled dendritic metal demands specialized solvent extraction, ion exchange, and vacuum metallurgy, representing extreme complexity and nation-state level capability.

upcoming_projects.reason: The project pipeline is strong relative to the thin market size, with multiple byproduct circuits under active construction in Canada and France alongside expanding lines in China and the Philippines. These facilities collectively add >20% to current global supply within 2–3 years.

india_position.reason:
Import Dependence: India has zero commercial domestic extraction of scandium. Latent processing options exist within IREL’s titanium and monazite waste streams, but no commercial recovery is operational, leaving domestic high-tech and defense needs 100% import-dependent.


Strategic Posture: Scandium is monitored under India's National Critical Mineral Mission and generic critical frameworks. However, no domestic extraction projects are assigned, no foreign equity holdings are secured, and no specific KABIL mandates exist, representing declared strategic intent at an early stage.

price_volatility.reason: Scandium oxide prices drifted down from $890–1,000/kg in 2021 to $640/kg in 2025 as new by-product supply entered the thin market (USGS), a 20–50% move on mid-range prices (Score 2). China, the leading producer, added scandium metal, alloys, oxides and compounds to its export controls in April 2025.

strategyList.name: Laterite nickel: RKEF and HPAL (Indonesia's route)
strategyList.what: RKEF furnaces smelt laterite into nickel pig iron, ferronickel or matte; HPAL leaches it in autoclaves into mixed hydroxide (MHP) for batteries.
strategyList.outside_china: Indonesia (67% of mined nickel; leads refining growth); Philippines (HPAL feed refined in Japan).
strategyList.cost: Vale-Huayou Pomalaa (Indonesia): US$4.5 bn for mine and HPAL making 120 kt/yr Ni and 15 kt/yr Co in MHP.
strategyList.india_base: No laterite at scale; Sukinda overburden; CSIR-IMMT 10 t/day proving plant; ferroalloy furnaces.

strategyList.name: Gallium recovery and high-purity refining
strategyList.what: Ion-exchange resins pull gallium from Bayer liquor; electrolysis and zone refining take it to 6N-7N.
strategyList.outside_china: China ~99% of primary output; ~9 t/yr elsewhere. New: Rio Tinto (Canada) pilot and demo; Alcoa (Australia, with Japanese and US partners) has a final investment decision.
strategyList.cost: Rio Tinto: C$26 m of public support for a pilot and a demo of up to 4 t/yr; commercial scale ~40 t/yr (~5% of world output).
strategyList.india_base: NALCO-HWB/BARC demo plant (Damanjodi, Nov 2025); C-MET 6N purification; NFC; Ion Exchange India resins.

strategyList.name: Scandium from residues
strategyList.what: Leaching red mud, TiO2 waste acid or HPAL streams; solvent extraction; precipitating scandium oxide.
strategyList.outside_china: China leads; Philippines and Japan (HPAL feed); Canada (Rio Tinto, from TiO2 waste).
strategyList.cost: Rio Tinto: ~C$25 m from the Canada Growth Fund toward 9 t/yr.
strategyList.india_base: NALCO fly-ash pilot (50 kg/day); red-mud pilot planned; CSIR-IMMT; CSIR-NML.

chemistryList.name: Ion-exchange resins
chemistryList.who: Ion Exchange India (Ankleshwar; hydrometallurgy and nuclear-grade resins); HWB-BARC's special resin.
chemistryList.carries_over_to: Gallium from Bayer liquor; scandium; heavy-REE polishing; lithium from brine.
chemistryList.fit: Direct for gallium (demo); adjacent for the rest
chemistryList.summary: Selective resin beads capture dissolved ions, then release them into a cleaner stream. India manufactures resins and has a gallium-recovery demonstration project, but each mineral application needs its own chemistry, feed testing and operating evidence.

links.how: Chelating resin can capture scandium from a suitable residue leachate while rejecting some bulk constituents. The 2024 primary study demonstrates why the actual leachate matters: useful column capacity was lower with contaminants than in simulated feed. It does not establish the economics of treating Indian red mud.
links.fit: Research-supported connection; Indian feed and economics require proof

chemistryList.name: Hydrometallurgy and process R&D
chemistryList.carries_over_to: Tellurium from slime; nickel from overburden; magnet and battery recycling; REE separation flowsheets.
chemistryList.summary: Hydrometallurgy dissolves and separates elements into useful products. India has process-development experience, pilot facilities and some industrial transfers. That foundation can support several mineral chains; each feed still needs its own validated flowsheet and commercial case.

links.how: Selective leaching and separation can investigate scandium-bearing residues. NML's register identifies a tin-slag project and a red-mud utilisation programme. Their existence supports a research link, not a claim that an Indian commercial scandium stream is already supplying customers.
